about: The end-to-end scenarios for a DataPipe deployment, as data rather than prose. site/index.html renders its "What to check" list from this file, and the e2e-testbed skill in the datapipe repo drives it. Add `experiment`, `base` and `run` to each scenario's params to build a URL.

defaults.resultContract: window.__testbed (schema 1); document.documentElement.dataset.testbedStatus and #testbed-result mirror it for drivers that cannot evaluate JavaScript.

preconditions.experiment: A fresh experiment on the deployment under test, storing to Google Drive (new experiments cannot choose OSF). Record its ID.
preconditions.dataCollection: "Accept new data" ON, except where a scenario says otherwise.
preconditions.conditions: "Assign conditions in sequence" OFF by default; the condition scenarios switch it.
preconditions.base64: "Accept base64 file uploads" OFF by default; the base64 scenarios switch it.
preconditions.metadata: Psych-DS metadata OFF by default. With it ON every expectStorage path below moves from the folder root to data/raw/.

timingFacts.sweepCron: */5 (staging sweep and upload retry share one scheduledsweep function)
timingFacts.note: A recovered session is QUEUED by the sweep, not uploaded by it. queue-upload.ts gives an entry with no provider error code nextRetryAt = now + 1 hour, and the retry worker runs on */5 -- so a partial file reaches storage roughly 65-75 minutes after the participant dropped out, not 15. For that hour the dashboard's queue panel describes it as an upload that did not go through. That is expected, not a bug.

scenarios.title: Clean finish
scenarios.description: jsPsych with save-as-you-go. The dashboard shows one session in progress with a running time while you work; it disappears when you finish, and exactly one file lands in storage.

notes: expect an `extension-pipe:` note only if something degraded

expectDashboard: While running: a "Sessions in progress" panel with one row reading "In progress" and a "Running for" value.
Within ~30 s of the page reporting finished: the panel is gone (it is only rendered while a session is open).
No queue panel.

expectStorage.naming: testbed-<run>-<stamp>-<pid>.csv, exactly the single name in __testbed.filenames
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkDashboardAfter: during the run, and again ~30 s after it finishes
timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Abandoned tab
scenarios.description: Close the tab half-way. Within seconds the dashboard row reads `Connection lost — may resume`; after 10 minutes, `Stopped — being recovered`; the sweep then queues the staged trials, and the `.partial.json` reaches storage about an hour later, not within 15 minutes.
driverActions: Open the URL in a new tab and let it run for about 20 seconds (~50 trials of 200).
Read window.__testbed once, and keep the filename from __testbed.filenames -- it is the only way to recognise the partial later.
Close the tab. Do not let the run reach its end.

notes: The page never reaches a terminal status: the tab is gone. The last status read before closing must be "running".
sessionId is null on this page -- extension-pipe does not surface it.

expectDashboard: Within seconds of the tab closing: the session row reads "Connection lost — may resume".
About 10 minutes later: "Stopped — being recovered".
Within about 15 minutes: the row is gone and a queue panel appears with the partial listed as "Retrying".

expectStorage.naming: <submitted filename without its extension>-<8 hex characters>.partial.json. The hash suffix is ALWAYS there -- partialFilenameFor derives it from the session id, not from a name collision.
expectStorage.completeness: partial: only the trials staged before the tab closed
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkDashboardAfter: immediately, at ~11 min, and at ~16 min
timing.checkStorageAfter: 65-75 minutes after the tab was closed

scenarios.deferredNote: Re-open the experiment's Drive folder 75 minutes after the tab was closed and look for one *.partial.json whose name starts with this run's filename stem. If the queue panel still shows it as "Retrying" before then, that is the 1-hour first-attempt delay, not a failure.

scenarios.title: Brief dropout
scenarios.description: Go offline for about 30 seconds mid-run, then back online, and finish. The dashboard row flips to `Connection lost — may resume` and back to `In progress`; you get one complete file and no partial.
driverActions: Open the URL and let it run for ~10 seconds.
Put the browser offline (DevTools network throttling, or the OS network toggle) for 30 seconds.
Go back online and let the run finish.

notes: an `extension-pipe:` note about a failed flush during the offline window is expected, not a failure

expectDashboard: During the offline window: "Connection lost — may resume".
After reconnecting: back to "In progress" (the reconnect slot heals the disconnect stamp).
After finishing: no in-progress row, no queue panel.

expectStorage.completeness: complete, with every trial including those recorded while offline
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkDashboardAfter: during the offline window and again after reconnecting
timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished
timing.note: The offline window must be under 10 minutes or the sweep will treat the session as abandoned.

scenarios.title: Failed final submission
scenarios.description: The page claims the filename first, so DataPipe refuses the real submission as a duplicate. The log shows the save failed, and the staged trials come back later as a `.partial.json` under a hash-suffixed name.
expectDashboard: An error panel naming FILE_EXISTS ("A file with this name already exists in the storage provider...").
Within about 15 minutes: a queue panel with the recovered partial as "Retrying".

expectStorage.naming: the pre-claim file under the run's own filename, plus <stem>-<8 hex>.partial.json holding the staged trials
expectStorage.completeness: the pre-claim file holds a placeholder line, not data; the partial holds the real trials
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)
expectStorage.note: api-data.ts deliberately does NOT discard staging on a duplicate-filename refusal -- that is what makes the partial recoverable.

timing.checkStorageAfter: the pre-claim file immediately; the partial 65-75 minutes after the run

scenarios.deferredNote: Re-check the folder ~75 minutes later for the .partial.json. The pre-claim file is there straight away and is not the thing under test.

scenarios.title: Ended early
scenarios.description: Set `abort` below the trial count and the experiment stops as a failed attention check would. The data is still submitted — the behaviour a save trial never had, because an aborted timeline never reaches one.

notes: a note reading "timeline ended early at trial 5 of 20"

expectDashboard: No in-progress row after the run; no error panel; no queue panel.

expectStorage.completeness: complete for what ran: 5 trial rows, not 20
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Baseline without streaming
scenarios.description: With save-as-you-go off there is one submission at the end, as before incremental upload existed. One file, and no in-progress row at any point.
expectDashboard: No "Sessions in progress" panel at any point -- nothing calls /api/session.
No queue panel.

expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Plain JavaScript, streaming
scenarios.description: The same recovery behaviour with no framework at all — an in-progress row while it runs, one file at the end. This was impossible until the staging client moved out of the jsPsych plugin.
driverActions: Open the URL, then press any key once (or dispatch a keydown) -- the page waits for a keypress before the trials start.

expectPage.sessionId: a non-empty string; this page, unlike the jsPsych one, can report it

expectDashboard: While running: one row reading "In progress".
After finishing: the panel is gone.

expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Plain JavaScript, uncompressed body
scenarios.description: The same run with gzip off, so the submission goes through the hosting layer as a plain JSON body. Worth running alongside the compressed one because gzip and the hosting rewrite are the two things in front of `/api/data` that can each break on their own.
driverActions: Open the URL and press any key once to start the trials.
expectDashboard: Identical to vanilla-streaming.

expectStorage.completeness: complete, byte-for-byte the same shape as the gzipped run
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Plain JavaScript, conditions
scenarios.description: With `Request a condition` ticked, the log shows the assigned number and the run proceeds normally.
driverActions: Switch "Assign conditions in sequence" ON in the experiment's "Data collection" panel and set "How many conditions?" to 2 before running.
Open the URL and press any key once to start.

expectPage.condition: an integer in 0..n-1; running twice in a row must give 0 then 1, since assignment is sequential
notes: a note saying the /api/condition request was made inside datapipe-client

expectDashboard: Nothing specific; the condition counter is not surfaced in the UI.

expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Plain JavaScript, condition assignment switched off
scenarios.description: Switch condition assignment off on the dashboard and run again: the page reports that `getCondition` threw and refuses to start, rather than running an unassigned participant.
driverActions: Switch "Assign conditions in sequence" OFF in the experiment's "Data collection" panel.
Open the URL. No keypress is needed -- the page stops before it asks for one.

expectPage.serverSide: POST /api/condition answers 400 with error CONDITION_ASSIGNMENT_NOT_ACTIVE. The page cannot see the status directly, because datapipe-client throws rather than returning it -- confirm the code with the direct probe in the skill's endpoint table if it matters.

expectDashboard: An error panel entry for CONDITION_ASSIGNMENT_NOT_ACTIVE.

scenarios.title: Duplicate rejection
scenarios.description: On the plain JavaScript page, sending the same file a second time is refused.
driverActions: Open the URL and press any key once. `resubmit=1` makes the page press "Send the same file again" itself; without it, click that button by hand.
expectDashboard: An error panel entry for FILE_EXISTS.

expectStorage.naming: the single name in __testbed.filenames -- the second request must not add a second copy or overwrite the first
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Closed experiment
scenarios.description: Switch data collection off and run the jsPsych test: no session is started and the final submission is refused with `DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE`.
driverActions: Switch "Accept new data" OFF in the experiment's "Data collection" panel and confirm the "Saved" flag appears.
Open the URL and let it run.
Switch "Accept new data" back ON afterwards if more scenarios follow.

notes: an `extension-pipe:` note that the session was refused; the page cannot see /api/session's status code itself

expectDashboard: No in-progress row at any point.
An error panel entry for DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE (logged twice: once by /api/session, once by /api/data).

scenarios.title: Base64 upload
scenarios.description: The plain JavaScript page sends a small valid base64 payload to `/api/base64`, which now runs inside the same consolidated function as `/api/data`. The decoded file lands alongside the run's data file.
driverActions: Switch "Accept base64 file uploads" ON in the experiment's "Data collection" panel first. Without it the endpoint answers 400 BASE64DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE before it ever looks at the payload.
Open the URL and press any key once.
expectDashboard: No error panel entry.

expectStorage.naming: the data file, plus <stem>.b64.txt holding the decoded text "testbed base64 payload"
expectStorage.location: the data file follows the metadata layout; the base64 file always goes to the folder root

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Base64 upload, invalid payload
scenarios.description: The same path with something that is not base64 at all. The endpoint refuses it with `INVALID_BASE64_DATA` and the run's own data file is unaffected.
driverActions: "Accept base64 file uploads" must still be ON: the active check runs BEFORE the validity check, so with it off this scenario returns the wrong code and proves nothing.
Open the URL and press any key once.
expectDashboard: An error panel entry for INVALID_BASE64_DATA.

expectStorage.location: experiment folder root (data/raw/ if metadata is on)

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished
